claims.title: Supplier paperwork may be intercepted on the unverified public-to-vendor upload path
claims.description: `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents` carries supplier staff contact details and compliance documents tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data` from `entity:supplier` to `process:supplier-portal` across a decided `boundary:public-internet` to `boundary:vendor-platform` crossing. Its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the unverified transport protection is absent or inadequate, an attacker able to observe this path can intercept the uploaded documents and contact details. The crossing relies on an inferred placement for `entity:supplier`, so public-network reach should also be confirmed. The disclosed records can be used to target suppliers and reveal the information later retained in `store:document-store`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents` crosses from the public-internet zone while its protocol and transport encryption are unstated, although an attacker still needs an on-path position. Impact is medium because the flow carries `pii` and `business-critical-data`, including supplier contact details and compliance paperwork.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce TLS for supplier uploads
mitigations.detail: Set a verified modern TLS posture for `flow:entity:supplier>process:supplier-portal>upload-documents`, including certificate validation and redirecting or rejecting plaintext access; document the protocol and `encryption_in_transit` attributes.

claims.title: Category-manager document reviews may be exposed on an unverified cross-zone connection
claims.description: `flow:entity:category-manager>process:supplier-portal>review-documents` crosses from `boundary:corporate-network` to `boundary:vendor-platform` and carries document reviews, approvals, and rejections tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`. Authentication, protocol, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the unverified transport confidentiality is absent or insufficient, an observer on the corporate-to-vendor path can intercept review activity and associated sensitive document context. That intelligence can identify supplier records and approval decisions later held by the vendor platform.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because this is a decided corporate-network-to-vendor-platform crossing with no verified protocol or transport encryption, but interception requires access to that path. Impact is medium because the flow is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data` and reveals supplier-document review decisions.

mitigations.detail: Use verified TLS for `flow:entity:category-manager>process:supplier-portal>review-documents`, document the protocol and encryption state, and require strong authenticated sessions for category-manager access.

claims.title: Uploaded documents may be visible on the unverified portal-to-document-store hop
claims.description: `flow:process:supplier-portal>store:document-store>store-documents` transfers uploaded compliance documents tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data` from `process:supplier-portal` into `store:document-store`. Its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If transport confidentiality is not actually present, an attacker with a position on this vendor-platform internal path can intercept the documents before storage. The capture exposes the same paperwork and staff details that remain available through `store:document-store`, without requiring a store read grant.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because protocol, authentication, and transport encryption are unverified, but an attacker must first obtain a position within the vendor-platform path. Impact is medium because the transferred documents are tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.detail: Require mutually authenticated TLS or an equivalent verified encrypted channel on `flow:process:supplier-portal>store:document-store>store-documents`, and obtain vendor evidence for the protocol, peer authentication, and encryption configuration.

claims.title: Nightly supplier extracts may be intercepted between the vendor platform and landing bucket
claims.description: `flow:entity:portal-vendor>store:landing-bucket>push-nightly-extract` crosses from `boundary:vendor-platform` to `boundary:cloud-account` while carrying the nightly supplier extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`. Its protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` remain unknown; the source says the extract "arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is," which does not establish channel encryption. If transport protection is absent or inadequate, an on-path attacker can intercept the complete nightly extract during delivery. The extracted records are then loaded by `process:supplier-master-service` and written to `store:supplier-database`, making a recurring interception a bulk source of supplier data.

quotes.text: The runbook for the landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:portal-vendor>store:landing-bucket>push-nightly-extract` is a decided vendor-platform-to-cloud-account crossing and has no verified protocol, authentication, or transport encryption, although interception requires path access. Impact is medium because each transfer is a supplier-data extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Use a verified encrypted and authenticated extract-delivery channel
mitigations.detail: Require TLS with authenticated vendor and cloud endpoints, or an equivalent managed private transfer mechanism, for `flow:entity:portal-vendor>store:landing-bucket>push-nightly-extract`; record and test its protocol, sender authentication, and encryption state.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the extract independently of its transport
mitigations.detail: Require the vendor to encrypt each extract to a cloud-account-controlled recipient key before transfer, so a captured transport artifact is not readable.

claims.title: Supplier-master retrieval from the landing bucket may expose the nightly extract in transit
claims.description: `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract` is a read path for the nightly supplier data extract, tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`. Protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If the service-to-bucket connection lacks effective transport confidentiality, an attacker positioned on that internal path can intercept the extract as `process:supplier-master-service` reads it. The captured data can then be correlated with the supplier records written to `store:supplier-database`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the path is within `boundary:cloud-account`, so an attacker needs an internal network position, even though protocol, authentication, and transport encryption are unverified. Impact is medium because the read flow carries a nightly extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.detail: Configure and verify TLS for `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract`, with workload identity authentication and bucket access restricted to the supplier master service.

claims.title: Supplier records may be exposed on the unverified service-to-database write path
claims.description: `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:supplier-database>write-supplier-records` carries supplier records tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data` into `store:supplier-database`. Protocol, authentication, and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If this internal connection is not confidential, an attacker able to observe the cloud-account path can intercept records during the nightly load. Those records persist in `store:supplier-database`, so recurring observation can build a copy of the supplier corpus.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because an attacker must obtain a position on an internal cloud-account path, although protocol, authentication, and transport encryption are all unverified. Impact is medium because the transferred supplier records are tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the database connection
mitigations.detail: Require verified TLS, preferably mutual TLS or workload-identity-bound database authentication, on `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:supplier-database>write-supplier-records`.

claims.title: A copied document-store artifact could disclose supplier documents if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:document-store` retains uploaded compliance documents and is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, but its data classification and `encryption_at_rest` are unknown. If the unknown encryption state resolves to no effective at-rest encryption, an attacker who obtains storage media or an operational copy of this store can read the documents without using `process:supplier-portal` or its user authentication path. This is conditional: it does not assert that the vendor store is unencrypted. The disclosure provides supplier contact information and compliance records that can support targeted fraud or social engineering.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown `encryption_at_rest` value: obtaining a storage-layer copy requires access to vendor operational media or copies, but no verified at-rest protection is recorded. Impact is medium because `store:document-store` holds `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Verify encryption at rest for vendor-held documents and copies
mitigations.detail: Obtain evidence that `store:document-store` uses strong encryption at rest with controlled key access, and that the same protection covers backups, snapshots, replicas, exports, and decommissioned media.

claims.title: A copied landing-bucket artifact could disclose the nightly extract if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:landing-bucket` holds the nightly supplier data extract and is tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, while its data classification and `encryption_at_rest` are unknown. If effective encryption at rest is not enabled, an attacker who obtains a copied bucket object, backup, snapshot, or underlying storage artifact can read the plain extract without authenticating through `process:supplier-master-service`. The disclosed file supplies bulk data that is subsequently loaded into `store:supplier-database`; this is conditional on resolving the at-rest encryption gap, not an assertion that the bucket is unencrypted.

quotes.text: The runbook for the landing bucket says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:landing-bucket` has no verified `encryption_at_rest` state and copied storage artifacts can be read outside the application path, though an attacker must obtain such a copy. Impact is medium because the bucket holds an extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt landing-bucket objects and operational copies
mitigations.detail: Enforce managed-key or customer-managed-key encryption at rest for `store:landing-bucket`, cover backup and replication paths, restrict object export permissions, and verify that arriving CSV files are encrypted before storage where feasible.

claims.title: A copied supplier-database artifact could disclose supplier records if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:supplier-database` contains supplier records tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`, but its data classification and `encryption_at_rest` are unknown. If this unresolved at-rest control is absent or ineffective, an attacker holding a database volume, snapshot, export, or backup can read supplier records directly rather than using a database application path. This is a conditional storage-copy threat and should be resolved by confirming encryption and key access rather than assuming the database is unencrypted.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:supplier-database` has no verified at-rest encryption and an attacker needs only a storage-layer copy rather than live database access. Impact is medium because the store holds supplier records tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Enforce encrypted database storage and protected copies
mitigations.detail: Verify and require encryption at rest for `store:supplier-database`, including backups, snapshots, exports, and replicas; restrict key use and export privileges to narrowly scoped operational roles.

claims.title: Code running in the supplier master service can read the entire landing extract through its existing access
claims.description: `process:supplier-master-service` reads `store:landing-bucket` through `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract`, which is explicitly a read flow carrying the nightly supplier data extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data`. An attacker who runs code in `process:supplier-master-service` can use the service's existing bucket access to read each arriving extract. The flow's authentication is unknown, so the scope and isolation of that access are unverified; this claim does not assume it is over-broad. The resulting extract can be correlated with the supplier records the service writes to `store:supplier-database`, enabling bulk disclosure outside the portal's normal user-facing path.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the attacker must first run code in the non-web `process:supplier-master-service`, whose exposure is unknown; the bucket-read flow's authentication and grant scope are also unverified. Impact is medium because that flow reads a nightly extract tagged `pii` and `business-critical-data` from `store:landing-bucket`.

mitigations.summary: Constrain and verify the supplier-master bucket identity
mitigations.detail: Use a workload-specific, short-lived identity for `process:supplier-master-service`, grant only the exact landing objects and time window it needs, and document the authentication on `flow:process:supplier-master-service>store:landing-bucket>load-extract`.
Log and alert on object reads, bulk downloads, and access from unexpected execution contexts for `store:landing-bucket`.
